We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being too much or not in this situation with my boyfriend. Let me start by laying out what's happening. First, my partner works full-time from 7 am to 7 pm. That's a long day, and I can imagine how exhausting that must be. I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9 am to 12 pm. We don't live together, but we're local, so we're always in and out of each other's homes. That seems like a good setup for maintaining a relationship without the pressures of living together. Now, my son decided he wanted to play football on weekends. He's 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially thinking of asking my boyfriend to pay for it, but when I mentioned it to my mum during a casual visit, she strongly expected me to pay and told me it was my responsibility, not my boyfriend's. That's interesting because my boyfriend has been in my life for three years, so I would have thought there's some shared responsibility. So, I ended up having to pay for it myself. To afford it, I extended my work hours to 9 am to 5 pm. That's a significant increase in my workload. Then, I asked my boyfriend if he could be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends. Given that he's at work until 7 pm, I can see why he might be hesitant. He looked uncomfortable and said, "Sorry, no can do. This is your dad's responsibility." I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in South London, while we live in North London, and his dad doesn't drive, whereas my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did, he wouldn't mind doing small stuff like this for me. I can see how that might have come off as demanding or even manipulative. I was trying to make a point about the practicality of the situation, but maybe I crossed a line. He got really angry and told me that he has to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games, etc., since I'm not home anyway. He said he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quickly. He then suggested that we break up because I was putting too many responsibilities on him. That's a strong reaction. I was shocked and responded by saying, "Really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world, love!" That probably didn't help the situation. The little sneak then went to see my mum and had a heart-to-heart with her, which ended up in her calling me and telling me I'm out of line. So, who is AITA (Ask a Terrible Adult) here? Is it me, or is it my boyfriend? Let's break this down. First, I asked my boyfriend to help with picking up and dropping off my son on weekends. Given his work schedule, it's understandable that he might not want to take on additional responsibilities, especially on his weekends. However, I extended my work hours to afford the football, which shows that I'm trying to take responsibility. But then, I snapped at him and made him feel guilty for not wanting to help, which might have pushed him away. On the other hand, he suggested breaking up over this, which seems like an overreaction. It's one thing to be upset about being asked to help, but quite another to end the relationship over it. My mum's involvement complicates things further. She told me it was my responsibility to pay for the football, which might have influenced my actions. But then she ended up telling me I'm out of line after talking to my son, which suggests that she thinks I'm being too demanding. So, am I AITA? Did I overstep by asking my boyfriend to help with my son's transportation? Or is my boyfriend AITA for overreacting and suggesting a breakup over this? I think it's a bit of both. I was trying to manage the situation by taking on extra work, but I handled the conversation with my boyfriend poorly. I snapped at him and made him feel guilty, which isn't fair. On the other hand, he reacted too strongly by suggesting a breakup over something that seems minor in the grand scheme of things. Maybe communication was the key issue here. If we had talked about our responsibilities and expectations more calmly and rationally, we could have found a solution without it escalating to a breakup suggestion. In the end, both parties could have handled the situation better. I should have approached the conversation more gently, and he should have expressed his feelings without threatening the relationship.
